metrics.quote: "OT threats don't keep office hours. Neither does SentryN3t."

showcase.headline: Your OT network is not an office network. Your cybersecurity shouldn't be either.
showcase.description: OT systems were never designed to be connected. PLCs, HMIs, and industrial sensors are invisible to traditional IT tools, and attackers know it. SentryN3t Protection monitors your industrial network in real time, using machine learning to detect behavioral anomalies across all OT, IoT, and IT/OT converged assets, before they become incidents.

cards.title: Real-Time Traffic Analysis
cards.description: Monitors every packet and flow across OT/IT segments, with no agents required on industrial devices

cards.title: ML Anomaly Engine
cards.description: ML models learn what's normal on your network and detect any deviation, including unknown threats

cards.title: Automatic Asset Inventory
cards.description: Discovers and classifies every connected device: PLC, HMI, RTU, IIoT sensors, legacy assets

cards.title: Actionable Alerts with Context and AI Assistant
cards.description: Explainable AI alerts with severity, affected asset, evidence, and assignable response workflow

cards.title: Multi-Tenant Architecture for MSSP
cards.description: Multi-tenant architecture ready for MSSP with strict per-client data isolation

cards.title: NIS2 Compliance Support
cards.description: Asset inventory, network visibility, and event traceability to support your NIS2 compliance

capabilities.headline: The Six Core Capabilities to Protect Industrial Infrastructure
capabilities.subheadline: From full asset visibility to regulatory compliance, in a single platform built for real OT environments.

items.title: OT/IoT Asset Inventory & Visibility
items.description: You can't protect what you can't see. SentryN3t auto-discovers and classifies every device on your network (PLCs, HMIs, RTUs, IIoT sensors, and legacy assets), agentless and without disrupting operations.

items.title: Signatureless Anomaly Detection
items.description: No signatures. Our AI engine learns the normal behavior of every device on your network and detects any deviation (unusual traffic, unknown connections, lateral movement), including threats never seen before.

items.title: OT Vulnerability & Exposure Management
items.description: Prioritize only the vulnerabilities that are actually exploitable in your environment. SentryN3t correlates your asset inventory with OT-specific threat intelligence so you act where it matters most.

items.title: Secure Remote Access for Vendors & Third Parties
items.description: Uncontrolled third-party access is one of the top OT attack vectors. Monitor and control remote access to industrial systems and detect unauthorized vendor connections before they create an incident.

items.title: Support for NIS2 Requirements
items.description: NIS2 requires knowing what assets you have, what's happening on your network, and being able to prove it. SentryN3t covers the technical pillars of that requirement (inventory, detection and event traceability) without replacing the compliance work your organization must own.

items.title: SaaS, On-Premise, or Air-Gapped Deployment
items.description: Many critical OT environments cannot connect to the cloud. SentryN3t deploys as SaaS, on-premise, or fully air-gapped, meeting the strictest security requirements of defense and critical infrastructure.

sectors.headline: Designed for Environments Where Failure Is Not an Option
sectors.subheadline: Every sector has its own protocols, assets, and regulations. SentryN3t Protection adapts to your operational reality.

items.name: Industry & Manufacturing
items.problem: An unplanned production halt costs tens of thousands of euros per hour. Protect PLCs, SCADA, and sensor networks from ransomware, lateral movement, and supply chain attacks.

items.name: Agri-Food
items.problem: Connected processing lines and cold chain systems are increasingly targeted in ransomware campaigns. OT cybersecurity for food and livestock industry.

items.name: Energy
items.problem: Continuity and resilience of essential services with 24/7 monitoring. Zero tolerance for unplanned outages under NIS2.

items.name: Healthcare
items.problem: Protection of connected systems and devices and continuity of care against OT/IoT threats in healthcare environments.

items.name: Supply Chain
items.problem: Control of suppliers and third parties: a central requirement of the NIS2 directive to reduce inherited supply-chain risk.

items.name: Public Administration
items.problem: ENS compliance, secure remote access, and citizen data protection in converged environments. Air-gapped deployment available for installations with sovereignty requirements.

items.name: Finance & Insurance
items.problem: Digital operational resilience and third-party risk management under DORA, with continuous visibility over critical connected systems.

sections.title: Principles applicable to the processing of personal data

blocks.text: Ewala applies the principles set out in article 5 of the GDPR to the processing of personal data:

rows.def: Personal data is processed lawfully, fairly and in a transparent manner in relation to the data subject.
Data is collected for specified, explicit and legitimate purposes and is not further processed in a manner incompatible with those purposes.
Data is adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary in relation to the purposes for which it is processed.
Data is accurate and, where necessary, kept up to date. Reasonable steps will be taken to ensure that inaccurate data is erased or rectified without delay.
Data is kept in a form which permits identification of data subjects for no longer than is necessary for the purposes of the processing.
Data is processed in a manner that ensures appropriate security through appropriate technical and organisational measures.

blocks.text: In the course of providing its cybersecurity, technological innovation and IT services, Ewala may act as a data processor on behalf of its customers, processing personal data in accordance with the customer’s documented instructions and the data processing agreement (DPA) signed between the parties.

In such cases, the customer acts as data controller and Ewala undertakes to comply with the obligations set out in article 28 of the GDPR, including the application of appropriate technical and organisational measures, limiting processing to the controller’s instructions, the duty of confidentiality of authorised personnel, the sub-processor regime, assisting the controller in complying with its obligations and the deletion or return of data at the end of the service, unless retention is required by law.
Ewala will not access or process its customers’ personal data for purposes other than those set out in the corresponding data processing agreement.

rows.def: Ewala IT Services S.L. (contact details in section 2).

Data comes from what is provided in the commercial and contractual relationship: quotes, contracts, invoices, requests, emails and any other communication arising from the customer relationship. The categories of data processed include: identification data (first name, surname, ID/tax ID, position), contact data (address, telephone, email), commercial data (services contracted, proposals, quotes), economic, financial and banking data (invoicing, payment method, payment history) and technical data arising from the provision of the service (IP addresses, activity logs, configurations).

Contracting of products and/or services and their management, provision and support of the contracted services, incident management, invoicing and collection, and preparation of aggregated and anonymised statistical reports on the company’s activity.

Performance of a contract or pre-contractual measures (art. 6.1.b GDPR), compliance with legal, tax and accounting obligations (art. 6.1.c GDPR) and legitimate interest in processing the data of contact persons of legal entities, sole traders and professionals (art. 6.1.f GDPR and art. 19 LOPDGDD).

Tax, accounting and labour advisers; the Spanish Tax Agency (AEAT) and other competent Public Administrations; financial institutions for the management of collections and payments; professionals and providers whose involvement is necessary to provide the service, with a data processing agreement in place; and, where legally required, State Security Forces and Bodies and Courts and Tribunals.
None are generally foreseen. Where they are necessary to provide the service, the safeguards described in section 12 will apply.

For the duration of the contractual relationship and, afterwards, for the periods legally established for compliance with tax, accounting and commercial obligations, as well as for the establishment, exercise or defence of legal claims.
No automated decision-making or profiling is carried out with customer data.

sections.title: Data protection information regarding data obtained through use and management of the Website

sections.title: Data protection information regarding the use of cookies

blocks.text: The Website uses cookies. The categories of data processed include online identifiers, browsing data and user preferences. Cookies that are not strictly necessary, such as Google Analytics analytics cookies, are only installed with the User’s prior consent.
The purpose, legal basis, categories of cookies used, recipients and how to manage them are detailed in the [Cookie Policy](/cookies), accessible through a link at the bottom of the Website.

In general, Ewala does not carry out international transfers of personal data, except those arising from the use of providers based in the United States: Netlify, Inc. and Resend, Inc., for handling the contact form, and Google LLC, for web analytics, the latter only if the User has given consent (see the [Cookie Policy](/cookies)).

Should personal data be transferred internationally as a result of its processing, such transfers will be carried out in accordance with applicable data protection regulations and, in particular, to countries whose level of protection has been declared adequate by an Adequacy Decision adopted by the European Commission, including, where the recipient has joined it, the EU-US Data Privacy Framework (Implementing Decision (EU) 2023/1795).

Where the European Commission has not adopted an Adequacy Decision for a given country or recipient, Ewala will adopt other safeguards provided for in data protection regulations, in particular by signing Standard Contractual Clauses, accompanied, where appropriate, by any supplementary measures that may be necessary.
Ewala informs data subjects of the existence of the following rights:

rows.def: To obtain confirmation of whether personal data concerning you is being processed and, if so, to access it and the information on the purposes of the processing, the categories of data, the recipients, the expected retention periods, the existence of other rights and the source of the data where it was not obtained from the data subject.
To obtain rectification of inaccurate personal data or completion of incomplete data.

To obtain erasure of data when it is no longer necessary for the purposes for which it was collected, consent is withdrawn, you object to the processing, the data has been unlawfully processed or must be erased to comply with a legal obligation.

To obtain restriction of processing when the accuracy of the data is contested, the processing is unlawful, the data is no longer needed by the controller but the data subject needs it for legal claims, or the data subject has objected to the processing.

To receive the personal data provided in a structured, commonly used and machine-readable format and to transmit it to another controller, where the processing is based on consent or on the performance of a contract and is carried out by automated means.

To object at any time, on grounds relating to your particular situation, to the processing of your personal data based on legitimate interest, as well as, in all cases and without needing to give reasons, to processing for direct marketing purposes.

rows.term: Right not to be subject to automated individual decisions
rows.def: Not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling, which produces legal effects or similarly significantly affects you.
To withdraw consent at any time, without affecting the lawfulness of processing based on consent before its withdrawal.

rows.term: Right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority
rows.def: Data subjects may lodge a complaint with the Spanish Data Protection Agency (AEPD) (C/ Jorge Juan 6, 28001 Madrid, Spain — [www.aepd.es](https://www.aepd.es)), especially where they have not obtained satisfaction in the exercise of their rights.

blocks.text: **How to exercise your rights**
Rights may be exercised before Ewala, free of charge, by either of the following means:

items: Letter addressed to: Ewala IT Services S.L., Calle Peña Brava 21, oficina 1B, PI de Silvota, 33192 Llanera (Asturias), Spain.

blocks.text: To exercise rights, the data subject must provide:

items: A signed written request stating the right they wish to exercise.
A copy of their identity document (national ID, passport or equivalent), only where there are reasonable doubts about the applicant’s identity.
If acting through a representative: documentation proving the representation (power of attorney, express authorisation or proof of parental authority or guardianship).

blocks.text: Ewala will handle requests within a maximum of one month from receipt, which may be extended by two further months in the case of complex or numerous requests, informing the data subject of the extension within the first month. Ewala may request additional information when necessary to verify the applicant’s identity or to locate the data covered by the request.
Ewala only requests personal data that is adequate, relevant and not excessive in relation to the purpose for which it is processed.

The User guarantees the truthfulness, accuracy, currency and authenticity of the personal data provided, and is liable for any damages that may result from breach of this guarantee. The User also undertakes to notify Ewala of any change or correction to their data through the means indicated in section 13.

Impersonation, adopting false identities, providing third-party data as one’s own and providing any untruthful data are expressly prohibited, and records made under such conditions may be cancelled, without prejudice to appropriate legal measures.

If the User provides personal data of third parties, they must first have informed those third parties expressly, precisely and unequivocally of the content of this Privacy Policy and have the necessary authority to provide such data.

In the event of non-compliance with this section, Ewala is exempt from any liability arising from the processing of data provided by the User in breach of legal requirements, the User being liable to Ewala or any third party for the damages caused.
Ewala’s Website and the services offered by the company are aimed exclusively at persons over eighteen (18) years of age with sufficient legal capacity to contract.

Ewala does not knowingly collect or process personal data of minors. If it becomes aware that data of a person under 18 has been collected without the consent of their legal representatives, it will delete it immediately.

If a legal representative becomes aware that a minor under their responsibility has provided personal data to Ewala, they may contact us at [rgpd@ewala.es](mailto:rgpd@ewala.es) to request its deletion.

If data of minors or persons without legal capacity is provided through the Website, the person providing it and acting on their behalf declares responsibly that they hold legal representation, parental authority or guardianship, or have the express authorisation of whoever holds it, and the company may require supporting documentation.
Legal representatives shall in any case be considered responsible for the acts of the persons in their care, in accordance with applicable regulations.

Ewala adopts and implements the technical and organisational measures necessary to guarantee the security of personal data, as required by article 32 of the GDPR, with the aim of ensuring the ongoing confidentiality, integrity, availability and resilience of processing systems and services.

The measures applied include, among others: encryption in transit and at rest, multi-factor authentication (MFA), access management based on the principle of least privilege, continuous monitoring, encrypted and verified backups, data leakage prevention measures, periodic access reviews, confidentiality agreements with all staff and periodic training in data protection and information security.
However, the User should be aware that security measures on the Internet are not infallible. Ewala will process personal data with due confidentiality and duty of secrecy.
Ewala shall not be responsible for the processing and subsequent use of personal data that may be carried out by third-party information society service providers acting outside the Website.

Ewala maintains a presence on professional social networks in order to inform users about its activity, products and services. The processing of personal data of those who follow the corporate profiles is based on the consent expressed by following those profiles or interacting with them (art. 6.1.a GDPR).

The processing of personal data carried out on those networks is also subject to each platform’s terms of use, legal terms and privacy policies, which Users are advised to consult. Ewala is not responsible for the processing carried out by the platforms themselves on their users’ data.

sections.title: Duration and modification of the Privacy Policy

blocks.text: The applicable Privacy Policy will be the one published on the Website at any given time. Ewala reserves the right to modify, in whole or in part, at any time, the content of this Privacy Policy by way of expansion, improvement, clarification or updating, whether due to legislative or case-law changes or changes in business strategy, without such modification having retroactive effect.
The Privacy Policy will always be accessible through a link at the bottom of the Website, indicating its version and publication date.

If any of the clauses included in this document is declared null, the rest of the document shall remain fully effective and binding on the same terms, provided it can subsist without the clause declared null.

The applicable law is Spanish law. Unless specific regulations establishing another jurisdiction apply, in particular consumer and user protection regulations, the parties submit to the Courts and Tribunals of Gijón (Spain) for any dispute, without prejudice to Ewala’s willingness to resolve any dispute amicably beforehand.

sections.title: Consent to the use of cookies

blocks.text: When you first access this website, a cookie notice is displayed that lets you decide freely on their use, with the same ease for accepting as for rejecting: you can accept them all, reject them all or configure your choice by category in the preferences panel. Rejecting cookies is as easy as accepting them.

No cookies other than technical or strictly necessary ones are installed until you give your consent. No pre-ticked boxes in favour of acceptance are used: if you save your choice without ticking any category, it is equivalent to rejecting all non-necessary cookies. Access to the website and its content is not conditional on accepting cookies.
Continuing to browse, scrolling the page or closing the notice without choosing are not, under any circumstances, valid ways of giving consent.

You can change or withdraw your consent at any time, as easily as you gave it, from the "Cookie preferences" link in the footer. Withdrawing it does not affect the lawfulness of processing carried out beforehand.
You will be asked for consent again 12 months after you gave or last renewed it, and also if the cookies used or their purposes change substantially.

Your choice and the date you made it are stored in a technical cookie (CookieConsent) in your browser. In addition, Cookiebot keeps a record of your consent (a random identifier, the date, the options chosen and your anonymised IP address) so that it can be proven, as required by the GDPR. Your choice applies only to the browser and device from which you make it, and to the ewala.es domain.
You can find more information about who we are, how to contact us and how we process your personal data in our [Privacy Policy](/privacidad), accessible from the footer.

A cookie is a small text file that is downloaded to your device (computer, phone or tablet) when you visit certain web pages. It allows the site to store and retrieve information about your visit: for example, remembering a preference you have chosen or counting how many people have read a page.

Besides cookies, there are other technologies with the same function (browser local storage, tracking pixels or device identifiers) and also fingerprinting techniques, which combine information to identify the device without needing to store anything on it. When this policy says "cookies", it refers to all of them.

Information obtained through cookies may constitute personal data when it allows you to be identified directly or indirectly; in that case, its processing is governed by our [Privacy Policy](/privacidad).

sections.title: What types of cookies are there?

blocks.text: Cookies are classified in three different ways, and each cookie belongs to one category in each group.
**By who manages them**

rows.def: Sent from equipment managed by the website owner.
Sent from equipment managed by another entity, which is the one that processes the data obtained.

blocks.text: **By how long they last**

rows.def: Deleted when you close the browser.
Remain on the device for the period indicated in the table, unless you delete them earlier.

blocks.text: **By what they are for**

rows.def: Allow browsing and the operation of the site, or save the choice you have made about other cookies. They are exempt from consent under article 22.2 LSSICE, because without them the service you requested cannot be provided.
Allow visits to be counted and how the site is used to be understood in aggregate, in order to improve content. They require your prior consent.
Allow browsing habits to be profiled in order to show personalised ads. This website does not use them.

sections.title: How can the use of cookies be managed on this website?

blocks.text: In the cookie preferences panel, accessible at any time from the "Cookie preferences" link in the footer, you can view all information about the cookies used (including their purpose, duration and whether they are first-party or third-party) and enable or disable those that are not strictly necessary for the site to work.

When you disable a cookie, it is removed from your browser whenever possible and, if it cannot be removed, it is blocked: a cookie you have rejected is never used. Some removal mechanisms depend on the third party responsible for the cookie and are outside our control.
Alternatively, you can block or delete cookies from your own browser settings, including third-party cookies you previously accepted. Note that this affects all websites you visit, not just this one:

items: Chrome: Settings → Privacy and security → Cookies and other site data.
Firefox: Settings → Privacy & Security → Cookies and Site Data.
Safari: Settings → Privacy → Manage Website Data.
Edge: Settings → Cookies and site permissions → Manage and delete cookies.

blocks.text: On mobile, the path is within the browser’s own settings, not the system settings.
This option can be exercised at any time. The panel and browser settings are specific to each device: if you want your choice to apply on another one, you will need to configure it there too.

sections.title: What happens if cookies are disabled?

blocks.text: Nothing that affects your visit. The site works the same, all pages remain accessible and the contact form is sent normally. The only effect is that your visit is not counted in our statistics.

If you block all storage from your browser, including technical storage, we may not be able to remember your choice and the notice may appear again on every visit. Under no circumstances does rejecting non-necessary cookies prevent access to the website or its essential content and services.

To the extent that information obtained through cookies constitutes personal data, you may exercise the rights of access, rectification, erasure, restriction of processing, portability and objection, as well as withdraw the consent given at any time, by writing to [rgpd@ewala.es](mailto:rgpd@ewala.es), under the terms set out in our [Privacy Policy](/privacidad).

You also have the right to lodge a complaint with the Spanish Data Protection Agency (C/ Jorge Juan 6, 28001 Madrid, Spain — [www.aepd.es](https://www.aepd.es)), especially if you have not obtained a satisfactory response when exercising your rights.

This Cookie Policy may be updated when the cookies used, applicable regulations or the criteria of supervisory authorities change. We recommend reviewing it periodically; the applicable version is always the one published on this page.

When significant changes occur in the cookies installed or their purposes, we will notify you through the website and you will be asked for consent again. If you have any questions, you can write to [rgpd@ewala.es](mailto:rgpd@ewala.es).
